Harish Belani vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 February,
2017
 Crr-273-2017
 (Harish Belani Vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh)
06-02-2017
Shri Kapil Sharma, learned counsel for the applicant.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Harish Belani Vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Shri Y. D. Yadav, learned Panel Lawyer for the respondent/State.
Heard on admission.
After perusing the impugned judgment and the memo of revision, I find this revision is arguable.
Hence, it is admitted for final hearing.
Learned Panel Lawyer has accepted the notice of admission of this revision on behalf of the respondent/ State.
Hence, no further notice is required to be sent to it.

Heard on I.A.
No.2200/2017, which is the first application under Section 397(1) of the Cr.P.C. moved on behalf of the applicant for suspension of post-conviction jail sentence and grant of bail to him during the pendency of this revision.

Vide the impugned judgment dated 25.1.2017 passed by the Special Judge and Additional Sessions Judge to the Court of First Additional Sessions Judge Raisen in Criminal Appeal No.235/2015 titled Harish Belani Vs. State of M.P. through Food Inspector Raisen, the sole applicant stands convicted under Section 7(1) r.w. 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act 1954 and sentenced thereunder to suffer RI for six months with a fine of one thousand rupees,
with default stipulation.

entities.text: Harish Belani Vs. State of M.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant remained on bail during trial of the case and also pendency of the appeal.
However, he has been undergoing the jail sentence since 25.1.2017, the date of the impugned judgment.
He submits that the applicant had already deposited the fine amount as imposed.
He submits that this revision is of the year 2017 and there is no likelihood of the same being listed for final hearing in recent future.

He submits that looking to the short term of remaining jail sentence, this revision becomes infructuous in case the applicant would have suffered the same before this revision being decided on merits.
He submits that the applicant has a good case on merits.
Upon these submissions, he prays to allow the I.A. Learned Panel Lawyer opposes the prayer.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the submissions raised on behalf of the parties by their counsel and the short term of jail sentence, but without commenting on merits of the case, I am of the view that it is a fit case for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the applicant, therefore, the IA is allowed.

The execution of remaining jail sentence of applicant Harish Belani is hereby suspended and it is ordered that he shall be released on bail upon his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of 30,000 (thirty thousand) rupees with one solvent surety of the same amount to the satisfaction of the trial Harish Belani vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 February, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137876697/
1 court, subject to depositing of fine amount, if any.

entities.text: Harish Belani vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On being released on bail, the applicant shall appear before the Registry of this Court to mark his presence first time on 29.8.2017 and thereafter on all such other dates as may be fixed by it in this regard until further orders of this Court.
Records of both the courts below be called for.
List the case for final hearing in due course.
Certified copy as per rules.
(RAJENDRA MAHAJAN) JUDGE ps
